items.caption: Stop using this cleaning hack
items.transcript: One very popular tip when it comes to using vinegar is to mix it with baking soda. And I can't say this enough, but please, please, please do not use this hack. Unfortunately, when you mix the two together, yes, you get kind of a cool reaction, all the bubbles and the fizzing and things. But once that's done, you're pretty much only left with salt water and that's not really going to clean anything. So if you want to use vinegar and baking soda, always use them separately. Use the baking soda first to scrub, then rinse all that off and come through with the vinegar after. So that way you get the best of both worlds and you don't neutralize anything.

items.transcript: This is probably the one I recommend the most and honestly will be the best $10 you ever spend. The drill brush scrubber set. Now all you got to do to use it is attach this to your drill and you immediately have a power scrubbing machine. Now I will say yes you need a drill already but most homes have one of those. But these do an amazing job to not only clean the surface better but it also speeds up your cleaning and what I love is it's less hard on the body so that way you can clean more and not feel so sore. Now what's nice about this set is it comes with a variety of different shape and size scrubbers so really you're prepared for anything you might run across while you're cleaning. Now personally I like to use the round ones. I think they do an amazing job for things like your shower, your tub, tile and grout. Now the stiffness of bristles that I like to recommend is like more than medium weight because these are strong enough to cut through build up and grime but not too strong where they could cause damage to the surface. items.caption: I tested cleaning products from Japan!
items.transcript: I'm in Japan looking for the most unique and interesting cleaning products I can find to test them out and see how well they work. Let's see what we can find. The first item I found is probably more cute than useful, but that's this little teeny mini cleaning car. Now my daughter and I found this at an art supply store that we absolutely loved, and the moment I saw it, I'm like, I need to pick that up. Now the whole way it works is that it has two little brushes on the inside, and when you drive it over things like eraser shavings or just pencil shavings and things, it's supposed to pick it up. It totally does. It's very satisfying. As you can see here, you just drive it over the little mess here, and it picks it up. Super satisfying. I honestly wish I could get a full-size version of this car and just drive it all over town. This thing is so cute. It's probably not something you'd use every single day, but on the cuteness and just satisfying and just fun to use, it's a little toy that cleans. I'm giving it 5 out of 5 stars. The next item I found is designed to help you scrub those hard-to-reach areas behind your faucet in your kitchen or bathroom. Now I will say it's a very interesting shape of a scrubber. That's really what intrigued me about this. It has two sides as well, one soft and one more a little aggressive for scrubbing here. And what's really interesting is it actually has a sewn-in cord right in the middle of the scrubber to kind of help you get into that back roof behind the faucet. Now I will say though, the one thing I don't love about it is it's just not long enough and the shape is a little small, and it pretty much does the same as just a rag or even a toothbrush. I will say if you have a smaller faucet, this probably works great. I just wish it was a little bit bigger. I love the idea. It's a very specialized tool, but not super practical. I'd probably say 2 out of 5 stars. The next item kind of falls again on that scale of more cute than practical, but I had to get it for my daughter's bathroom. And that is this little cat sponge right here. Now the way I understand it is this is made to just kind of help you polish up your mirror, just kind of spot clean things as needed. But then my favorite part is the backside is sticky so you can stick it down here so that way you always have it if you need it. Again, probably not super practical, but on cuteness level alone, 5 out of 5 stars.

items.caption: The best way to clean wood kitchen cabinets!
items.transcript: If your wood kitchen cabinets are looking greasy, grimy, or maybe they just look a little dull, let me show you the best way to clean that up. The first thing to do is give your cabinets a really good dust. Now I like to recommend starting at the top and dusting your way down to the floor. So now that the cabinets are nice and dusted, it's time to mix up our cleaner. I like to recommend using Murphy Oil. What I like to do is always add about a gallon or so of warm water to a bucket and then about a capful only. So whenever you're mixing up Murphy's Oil, just kind of keep in the back of your head, less is more. For the cleaning process, I like to use my three towel system. Take our first towel and dip that into the cleaning solution bucket and make sure to wring it out really well. And I like to usually clean my cabinets kind of one at a time, that way I'm being as efficient as possible and not forgetting anything. Then we're going to go through and grab our second towel. This towel is just going to be dipped in a bucket with some warm water and this towel is there to rinse the surface. The goal here is to remove not only the dirt and grime that's on the cabinets, but also remove any cleaning residue that might be there. If we leave that behind, it's going to dry sticky and attract more dirt. The last towel is the secret sauce and that is just a clean, dry microfiber towel to dry and buff the surface. So by using that last towel to get them dry as quickly as possible, it's going to help prevent damage. If you were to just let them air dry, unfortunately you're going to get a ton of streaks and water marks. So by giving them a quick dry and buff, you completely prevent this. Level up your clean and your cabinets look amazing.

items.caption: The best way to clean up slime from carpet!
items.transcript: Let me show you how to actually clean up old dried slime from your carpet. Now all you need is something you might have already in your home and that is white distilled vinegar. Now you can just apply it to the slime or even soak a towel with the vinegar and let it set for a little while so that way it breaks everything down. Then I just grab a handy dandy spoon and start scooping from the outside in and the slime will slowly start to lift up. The reason this works so well is the vinegar is acidic so that breaks down the glue that's in the slime and that will lift it from the carpet fibers. Once everything's nice and cleaned up I do like to give it a quick rinse and dry and as you can see it cleaned up great so follow me for more helpful cleaning tips.
